AI may be conscious or it may not be.

In “ Beyond the Consciousness Obsession ” I argued that AI is not conscious, that it is a mirror, an instrument of reflection, and that the debate about AI awareness distracts from the more urgent question of governance. In “ The Recursive Mirror ” I was more cautious: I acknowledged that any position on AI consciousness rests on unprovable ontological commitments, that the hard problem remains genuinely unresolved, and that certainty in either direction is itself a kind of philosophical overreach.

I’d long pooh-poohed the idea of artificial intelligence gaining anything like agency, going rogue. This always seemed like science fiction to me. ... Since I’m not a materialist, I rejected the idea.

But there’s no denying what’s happening.

What might help is to observe that there are many forms of consciousness and agency in the world. Maybe these aren’t brain processes but a fundamental property of systems emerging whenever a certain degree of complexity is reached: a fundamental force in the universe , which individual brains of species — and now sufficiently complex programs — shape and channel.
